summary: Audited pages #13 (07-gas-bill-too-high), #14 (25-utility-bill-taxes-fees-franchise-charges-explained), #15 (stormwater-fee-on-water-bill-explained), #16 (average-utility-bills-by-state-2026). Verified contradictory national average claims across site, Hawaii arithmetic error in #16's table, and confirmed #13 has zero sourced dollar figures despite affiliate monetization.
findings: CRITICAL-CONTRADICTION #16 (average-utility-bills-by-state-2026.md): National average narrow basket claimed as ~$262/month (line 22) but arithmetic gives ~$324 (electric $159 + gas midpoint $80 + water/sewer midpoint $85). $262 claim is unsupported and contradicts site's own 2026-utility-cost-index-by-state.md which also claims $262 but different methodology.

CRITICAL-CONTRADICTION cross-page: 2026-utility-cost-index-by-state.md line 25 explicitly says Hawaii electric bill is '$200-$240 — not $450,' but the $450 figure does not appear on #16's current version — it appears as a refuted claim on another page, suggesting author awareness of the error but failure to reconcile.

ERROR #16 Hawaii table arithmetic: 900 kWh × 33.7¢/kWh (page's stated Hawaii rate) = $303.30, but table shows $275* for Hawaii electric. This understates Hawaii electric by ~$28. Note acknowledges this by saying 'standardized 900 kWh' but $275 is still wrong — it should be $303 if using page's own rate.
ERROR #16 National electric: Page claims $159/month at 18.34¢/kWh for 900 kWh. 900 × 0.1834 = $165.06, not $159. Off by $6.06 (3.7%).

CRITICAL-C0 #13 (07-gas-bill-too-high.md): Zero sourced dollar figures despite monetization. Savings table (lines 258-266) lists 8 fixes with specific monthly dollar savings and payback periods — none sourced. The 6 listed sources (1 EIA, 5 energy.gov) are generic background URLs that do not support any specific dollar claim on the page. Affiliate product box for Nest Thermostat (line 331) is monetized but its savings claim (~12% heating, ~15% cooling) is unsourced. Violation of P0 item S3b.

VERIFIED #16 broad basket $430-500 claim: Not verifiable from EIA RECS data. EIA tracks electricity, gas, not bundled internet/trash/sewer. $430-500 appears to include estimated internet ($60-80), trash ($15-35), and full water/sewer. No sourced data for these adders. Claims 'based on EIA, AWWA, state PUC reports' but AWWA's Water & Wastewater Rate Survey (typically $40-60/mo for water alone for 7,500 gal) is not cited with URL. NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW.

NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW Hawaii actual consumption: Page correctly notes Hawaii ~515 kWh/month (line 266 note citing EIA FAQ). EIA FAQ (retrieved 2026-08-29) confirms Hawaii lowest at 6,178 kWh/year = ~515 kWh/month. The standardized 900 kWh figure is therefore an overestimate for Hawaii by 75%, inflating the state's total. Note should be more prominent.

ISSUE #16 table is partial: Only 17 of 50 states shown despite claim of 'state-by-state breakdown.' Heading says 'full comparison' and 'every U.S. state' (line 37-38) but table is a sample. This is a significant completeness gap. Partial table of 17 states shown; 33 states unsurveyed.

DIAGNOSIS #14 (25-utility-bill-taxes-fees-franchise-charges-explained.md) 6-second time-on-page: Page is 100% procedural — it tells readers to 'check their bill and tariff' without providing any dollar amounts, examples, or actionable estimates. 324 words total (shortest page in audit set). No unique value vs other site pages. The 6s TOP (vs site median ~40s) suggests users see no useful content and bounce. Recommended fix: add 3-5 real-world examples with cited state-specific fee ranges (e.g., typical franchise fee 3-5%, gross receipts tax 1-3%).

ISSUE #15 (stormwater-fee-on-water-bill-explained.md) draft: true but still live/visible? Check Hugo config — if draft pages render in production, this is leaking unfinished content. National average $12/quarter cited from 'Rainplan data' (line ~170) — no URL, UNVERIFIED. Regional cost examples cite Raleigh ($8.22/month, line ~157) without current URL. 'Fort Worth FY26 increase brings $3.4M' (line ~183) — needs source.

WEAK COPY #13: 'Every degree above 68°F increases heating energy use by roughly 3-5%' — the DOE source says 1-3% per degree. Claim of 3-5% is inflated by ~67%. No source given for this specific range.

WEAK COPY #16: '60-70% of natural gas usage in a typical home' for heating — EIA says 43% (2020 RECS: space heating 43% of site energy, water heating 28%, appliances 29%). The 60-70% claim is overstated and unsourced.
